title: Commutative decomposition of infinite symmetric groups and transformation monoids
summary: The commutative subgroup width of a group $G$ is the smallest $k$ such that there are abelian subgroups $A_0,A_1,\ldots,A_{k-1}\leq G$ with $G=A_0A_1\cdots A_{k-1}$. Commutative (inverse) submonoid width is defined analogously. In 2002, Abért showed, rather surprisingly, that the commutative subgroup width of the symmetric group on an infinite set is always finite. It was later shown by Seress that it is always bounded above by $14$.
